situations: gone while the window is open

rows.does: Uses the defaults and writes the file at the first save.
rows.says: nothing: a first start is no fault

rows.does: Reads again three times, a tenth of a second apart; a file still held gives the defaults for this run, and no save of this run writes over it.
rows.says: The settings file could not be read, so the defaults are used. <path>: <the system's reason> Settings are not saved in this run, so that the file is not replaced. Close the window and start it again.

rows.does: Keeps what was changed until the window closes, logs every failed save and says it once in a run: a notice in a window, a system line in a console window.
rows.says: Settings could not be saved: <the system's reason>. What you change lasts until this window closes.

rows.does: One value that does not read is put to its default alone and named, the rest of the file is loaded, and the file as it was is copied once beside it with .bad at the end of its name.
rows.says: The settings file was read, except for the settings named here. <path>: these settings were not understood and are at their defaults: <the names>. A copy is kept as <path>.bad.

rows.does: A file whose text is no JSON object gives the defaults, and the file as it was is copied once beside it with .bad at the end of its name before the next save writes the defaults.
rows.says: The settings file could not be read, so the defaults are used. <path>: <the reader's reason> A copy is kept as <path>.bad.

rows.does: A stored window place that lies partly or wholly off the screens is fitted into the working area of the screen it shares the most with; one on no screen is dropped and Windows places the window.
rows.says: nothing: the window opens where it can be seen

rows.does: A model name that is not letters, digits, dots, hyphens and brackets is replaced by the fast model at the load and again where the command line is made; the log holds its length.
rows.says: nothing: the default model answers

rows.does: A save keeps what the file gained since this window loaded it: each top-level setting keeps the file's value unless this window changed it, and a list both windows changed is this window's whole.
rows.says: nothing: nothing is lost that needs an answer

rows.does: Members this version does not know are kept and written back as they were, under no seal.
rows.says: nothing: the newer version finds its settings again

rows.does: The consent file and the recently closed list keep the members this version does not know and write them back.
rows.says: nothing: the newer version finds them again

rows.does: A consent file that is no JSON counts as nothing agreed, so each access layer asks again before it connects to its program.
rows.says: nothing by itself: the reminder before the first connection is shown again

rows.does: A missing recently closed list is an empty list; the Window menu offers nothing to open again.
rows.says: nothing: an empty list is no fault

rows.does: An entry of the recently closed list that is not a whole path is neither read nor written, so no entry can be taken as an option of a command line.
rows.says: nothing: the entry is left out

rows.does: The recently closed list is read, added to and written by one window at a time, under a mutex named after the file; a window that waits more than half a second writes nothing, and the log holds a line.
rows.says: nothing: every window's entry ends up on the list

rows.does: A writer of the recently closed list that cannot get its turn within half a second gives up without hanging the window that closes.
rows.says: nothing: the log holds a line

rows.does: Without a theme file every window is painted with the system's colours; Reload theme says how to make one.
rows.says: No theme file: axKit menu, Theme, Edit theme file makes one
rows.proof: tests/scripts/axDown/10-theme.txt: Reloading with no theme file says how to make one

rows.does: A theme file that is no JSON or no theme file is not used: the windows keep the system's colours, the log says why once, and Reload theme says so.
rows.says: No theme: the file is not a theme file; the log says why

rows.does: A colour of the theme file that does not read is the system's colour, and Reload theme counts and names the values not understood.
rows.says: Theme reloaded: 1 value not understood, <the value's name>

rows.does: A missing reports settings file gets a new reporter id at the first report, kept from then on.
rows.says: nothing: the id is made without a question

rows.does: Starts the default shell, uses none of the shells of the file, keeps the other settings, and keeps the file as it was found beside it with .changed at the end of its name; said once, as a system line.
rows.says: Your shells in axTerminal's settings were changed outside axKit and are not used. Add them again from Session, Add a shell. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: Trusts no repository, so git runs none of their own programs, keeps the other settings, and keeps the file as it was found beside it with .changed at the end of its name.
rows.says: The repositories you trusted in axGIT's settings were changed outside axKit and are not used: git runs none of their own programs. To trust one again, open it and choose Trust this repository. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: A trusted repository whose own programs are not the ones it named when it was trusted is not trusted for them: its programs stay off and the notice asks again.
rows.says: This repository runs programs of its own (the notice's title, then the programs by name)

rows.does: Offers none of the custom programs of Open with, keeps the other settings, and keeps the file as it was found beside it with .changed at the end of its name.
rows.says: Your programs of Open with in axFile's settings were changed outside axKit and are not used. Add them again from Options, Add a program to Open with. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: Lists none of the user's own servers, keeps the other settings, and keeps the file as it was found beside it with .changed at the end of its name.
rows.says: Your servers in axMCP's settings were changed outside axKit and are not used. Add them again with Ctrl+N at the top level. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: Does not use the place of Claude Code named in the file and looks for Claude Code in the usual places; the other settings stay.
rows.says: The place of Claude Code in axClaude's settings, claudePath, was changed outside axKit and is not used: axClaude looks for Claude Code in the usual places. If it is not found, choose it again with Locate claude.exe in the notice that says so. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: AI help reads as off, with no folder Claude may read, the usual search for Claude Code and the default working folder; the model is kept. The next thing that needs the settings shows the notice AI help and does not go on with what was asked.
rows.says: AI help's settings were changed outside axKit and are not used: Claude is off, it may read no folder of yours, and Claude Code and its working folder are the usual ones. Turn Claude on and add the folders again from the axKit menu, Claude. The file as it was found is kept beside it, with .changed at the end of its name.

rows.does: An agreement that something other than axKit wrote into the consent file is no agreement: nothing counts as agreed, and each access layer asks again.
rows.says: The record of what you agreed to was changed outside axKit and is not used, so axKit asks again.

rows.does: The AI tools read as off with no paired tool; the axKit menu's AI tools submenu says why at every opening until the tools are turned on again or forgotten, and the log holds it once in a process.
rows.says: The AI tools' setting was changed outside axKit, or its key is gone: AI tools are off, and every AI tool must be allowed again.

rows.does: The list of the files accepted in Claude's working folder is not used when it was changed by hand or by another program: every obeyed file is asked about again.
rows.says: The list of files accepted in Claude's working folder was changed outside axKit and is not used: every such file is asked about again. (in the log; the window shows the notice of the files)

rows.does: The list of the reports the report form wrote is not used when it was changed outside axKit, and taking the file away does not bring back the time before it: no report saved before then is sent.
rows.says: The list of the reports axKit's report form wrote was changed outside axKit and is not used: reports saved before now are not sent. (in the log; the window says how many files were not sent)

rows.does: A save takes another window's shells from the file only when the file's seal checks; from a file whose seal does not check it takes nothing.
rows.says: nothing: the merge needs no answer

rows.does: A key file of the settings' seal that is there and cannot be read refuses every sealed setting until a save makes a new key.
rows.says: the refusal sentence of each sealed file, as in its own row

rows.does: A sealed file whose key file is gone is refused: its sealed settings are at their defaults until they are set again through axKit.
rows.says: the refusal sentence of each sealed file, as in its own row

rows.does: A hotkey that cannot be registered at a start shows the window once with a notice, so that the app can still be reached and another key chosen.
rows.says: The hotkey <key> is taken by another program. Options, Hotkey, to choose another.
rows.owed: a window script in which another process holds the hotkey before the app starts; no script registers a key of its own yet

rows.does: A new hotkey chosen in the Hotkey notice that another program holds is not taken, and the old key stays registered.
rows.says: <key> is taken by another program
rows.owed: a window script in which another process holds the key that is chosen in the Hotkey notice

rows.does: A remembered path that is not on a drive of this computer is not looked at during a start: the window opens on its fallback and says the path was not opened.
rows.says: <path> is on the network and was not opened at start; Open recent opens it.

rows.does: No window asks whether a remembered path exists except through LocalPaths, which asks only of a path on this computer; a path elsewhere is listed as it is and found missing when it is chosen.
rows.says: nothing while listing

rows.does: Save of a file another program changed since it was opened asks first: Write over, Reload and lose mine, or Cancel.
rows.says: The file changed on disk (the notice's title). <name> was changed by another program since you opened it. Write over it, or reload it and lose your changes?
rows.proof: tests/scripts/axDown/03-files.txt: Saving a file that another program changed asks first

rows.does: On coming back to the window, a file changed on disk is read again with the caret kept on its line when nothing is unsaved; with unsaved changes it is said once and Save will ask.
rows.says: Reloaded, <name> changed on disk; or, with unsaved changes: <name> changed on disk; Save will ask
rows.owed: a window script that activates the window after the change (a test window is never activated), or the step by ear of docs/axDown/nvda-test-plan.md

rows.does: An item file that does not read as an item is a row of its list, named by its file, which Enter opens in axJSON; Rename and Delete leave it alone.
rows.says: <file name>, not readable as an item, Enter opens it in axJSON
rows.proof: tests/scripts/axTask/10-damaged-item.txt: Hear a damaged item in its list

rows.does: An action key of a list that moves or opens, and that this install neither wrote nor accepted, says what it now does at the first press and acts at the second; a key that sets fields acts at once.
